ZeniMax Media was a Rockville, Maryland video game holding company that owned Bethesda Softworks and studios including Bethesda Game Studios (The Elder Scrolls, Fallout), id Software (Doom), Arkane, MachineGames and ZeniMax Online Studios. It sold games to consumers globally through publishing and online subscriptions. Founded in 1999, it was acquired by Microsoft in March 2021 for about 7.5 billion dollars and now operates within Xbox Game Studios. Its franchises have very high consumer awareness worldwide, but the corporate name itself is little known to the public.

Ziff Davis is a New York digital media and internet company, listed on Nasdaq (ZD). It owns a portfolio of web brands and services, including IGN, Mashable, PCMag, CNET, Everyday Health, Speedtest by Ookla, and cybersecurity, email marketing and cloud businesses. Revenue comes from advertising, subscriptions, lead generation and licensing, serving consumers and technology and healthcare marketers. It has over a billion monthly visits across its sites and annual revenue around 1.4 billion dollars. Several of its media brands, especially IGN and CNET, are well known to tech and gaming audiences.

Ag Growth International is a Winnipeg, Manitoba maker of grain handling, storage, conditioning and food processing equipment, including Westeel bins, Wheatheart augers and Hutchinson conveyors. Customers are farmers, grain handlers, ethanol and food processors across North America, Brazil, Europe and other markets. Revenue is roughly 1.4 billion Canadian dollars a year. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (AFN). It is an industrial B2B business selling mainly through dealers, with little consumer brand awareness outside agriculture.

Assent is an Ottawa-based software company providing cloud supply chain compliance and sustainability software. Its platform helps manufacturers and retailers collect data from suppliers on product regulations, conflict minerals, forced labor, PFAS, ESG and trade rules. Customers are mid-size and large industrial, electronics, medical device and consumer product manufacturers, paying subscriptions. It was founded in 2008 and has raised around 530 million dollars, including a large round led by Vista Credit and others. It is a B2B brand with little public consumer awareness.

Behalf was a New York fintech offering B2B payments and short-term financing, letting small and mid-size businesses buy from suppliers on net-30 to net-90 terms while the supplier is paid upfront. It earned fees from buyers and suppliers on financed purchases. Founded in Israel around 2012, it grew into a US-focused platform and raised about 462 million dollars including debt facilities. Its last disclosed round was in July 2021. It is a B2B brand with limited public awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Capital Funding Group is a Baltimore, Maryland, specialty finance firm providing financing to healthcare real estate and operators, notably skilled nursing and senior living facilities, through lending including HUD-insured loans, bridge and working capital finance, and advisory services. Customers are owner-operators of long-term care and healthcare facilities across the United States. It lists around 500 million dollars in funding or debt capital, most recently in April 2025. It is a B2B lender with low public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cox Communications is a US cable and broadband provider, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia and serving residential and business customers in about 18 states. It sells internet (Cox Internet, Panoramic Wifi), TV, home phone, home security and commercial network and cloud services, with annual revenue near 13 billion dollars. It is the largest private broadband company in the US, part of Cox Enterprises, a family-owned group that also controls Cox Automotive and Manheim. In 2025 it agreed to merge with Charter Communications. A visible regional consumer brand.

De Nora is a Milan-based technology company designing electrodes, coatings and electrochemical systems used in chlorine production, water treatment, pool filtration, electronics and green hydrogen. Its brands include Industrie De Nora, Sanitec and Capital Controls. Customers are industrial, municipal and energy companies worldwide, with revenue around 800 million euros and global manufacturing. Founded in 1923, it listed on Euronext Milan (DNR) in 2022. The Nora family and Snam hold large stakes. It is a B2B business with low consumer awareness.

Deem is an Oakland, California technology platform for the business travel industry, offering cloud tools for corporate travel booking, itinerary management and expense reporting, along with a marketplace for travel suppliers. Customers are corporates and travel agencies, with revenue from subscriptions and transaction fees. It grew out of Rearden Commerce, founded in 2000 and rebranded Deem in 2013, and raised about 536 million dollars, last in 2016. It is private and a B2B brand with limited public awareness.

DriveWealth is a New York fintech offering embedded investing infrastructure via APIs: fractional share trading, brokerage, custody and clearing for apps and brokerages. Clients include Cash App, Revolut, Stash and other fintechs, with global reach across more than 100 countries. Founded in 2012, it raised about 540 million dollars, including a 2021 round led by Softbank that valued it around 2.8 billion dollars. It earns fees on trading and balances. It is a B2B platform with limited consumer recognition, though its partners' apps are well known.

Druva is a Santa Clara, California cloud data protection company offering a SaaS platform for backup, disaster recovery, ransomware protection and data resilience across endpoints, servers, SaaS apps and cloud workloads, built on AWS. Customers are enterprises worldwide that pay subscriptions. Founded in 2008 in Pune, India, it has raised around 475 million dollars, with a valuation of about 2 billion dollars in 2021, and serves more than 6,000 customers. It is private and has limited public brand awareness outside IT circles.

Emeren, formerly ReneSola, is a solar project developer and independent power producer headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut. It develops, builds, owns and sells utility-scale and distributed solar and storage projects across the US, Europe and Asia, with a development pipeline measured in gigawatts and a small owned portfolio generating electricity revenue. It started as a Chinese solar wafer maker founded in 2005 and rebranded in 2022. It was listed on the NYSE and Nasdaq under SOL, and agreed to be taken private in 2025. It has low consumer awareness.

FLO is a Quebec-based electric vehicle charging network operator and manufacturer. It designs and builds Level 2 and DC fast chargers, runs a public network across Canada and the US, and sells hardware, software and services to utilities, retailers, municipalities and fleet and home customers. It was founded in 2009 and has raised roughly 470 million dollars, including investment from Investissement Quebec and Fonds de solidarite FTQ. It is private. Visible among EV drivers in Canada, with limited wider awareness.

Fuze was a cloud unified communications and collaboration provider, based in Campbell, California, offering cloud voice, video meetings, messaging and contact center for enterprises. Founded in 2006 as ThinkingPhones, it raised roughly 530 million dollars in funding. It was acquired by 8x8, a cloud communications company listed on the NYSE, for about 250 million dollars in 2021 and its customers were folded into 8x8. It was a B2B brand with limited public awareness and no longer operates independently.

HoneyBook is a San Francisco software company offering an all-in-one client management platform for independent businesses and freelancers such as photographers, planners, designers and consultants. Its tools cover bookings, proposals, contracts, invoicing, payments and scheduling, with subscription revenue plus payment fees. Founded in 2013 in Israel and the US, it raised around 500 million dollars with a valuation of 2.4 billion dollars in 2021 and serves hundreds of thousands of small businesses. It is private, mainly a US small business brand, with moderate awareness among creative freelancers.

Huimin is a Beijing B2B e-commerce platform focused on small neighborhood retailers and convenience stores in China. It supplies fast-moving consumer goods such as food, drinks and household products, linking brands and distributors to small shops through online ordering and logistics. Its parent is associated with the Huimin group of retail supply platforms. It raised about 520 million dollars, most recently in September 2019. It is a B2B business with little brand awareness outside China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Kaseya is a Miami, Florida IT and security management software company. Its platform serves managed service providers and IT teams with remote monitoring and management, backup, security, PSA and IT documentation tools, including Datto, which it acquired in 2022, and brands such as Unitrends, IT Glue and Spanning. Customers are MSPs and small and mid-size businesses globally, paying subscriptions. It is private, backed by Insight Partners, TPG and others, and sponsors sports properties. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

Kilter Finance is a London-based specialty finance company providing financing, according to Crunchbase, to financial services and asset-backed borrowers, with about 500 million dollars of capital reported in April 2020. It operates in the United Kingdom as a non-bank lender. Its customers appear to be businesses rather than consumers, and it raises funds from institutional investors. Public detail is thin and it has little brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Loscam is a Hong Kong-headquartered pallet and returnable packaging pooling company that rents wooden and plastic pallets and containers to manufacturers, FMCG suppliers and retailers. It operates across Asia Pacific, with depots in Australia, New Zealand, China, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia and elsewhere, and a fleet of tens of millions of units. It originated in Australia and is owned by private equity and infrastructure investors, with a 2025 financing round of roughly 470 million dollars shown. B2B with low consumer awareness.

Lyric Capital Group is a Charleston, South Carolina investment firm that provides capital to songwriters, artists and composers by acquiring and managing music catalog and intellectual property rights. Its Crunchbase profile shows about 500 million dollars raised in October 2021. It earns income from royalties on streaming, radio, licensing and sync. Customers are music rights holders and artists. A niche financial and IP investor with low public awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Medbanks is a Shanghai health data company operating a database platform of clinical and research information, used by hospitals, pharma and biotech companies for oncology and other clinical research, trial recruitment and data services. Customers are healthcare institutions and life sciences firms in China. It raised about 536 million dollars, most recently in February 2021. It is a B2B business with no consumer brand awareness outside China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Own Company, formerly OwnBackup, is a data protection and management platform headquartered in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey. Its software backs up, restores and secures SaaS data, mainly Salesforce, with archiving and seeding tools, serving thousands of enterprise customers. It was founded in 2015 and acquired by Salesforce in 2024 for about 1.9 billion dollars, and has raised around 507 million dollars as an independent. B2B subscription revenue. Brand awareness is limited outside Salesforce administrators.

Plus, formerly PlusAI, is a Santa Clara, California developer of autonomous driving software for heavy trucks. Its SuperDrive system targets driverless long-haul trucking, with partners including Traton, Hyundai, Iveco and others. It was founded in 2016 and raised about 490 million dollars. In 2025 it agreed to go public through a SPAC merger with Churchill Capital IX, targeting a Nasdaq listing. B2B customers are truck makers and fleets, with little consumer awareness.

Shanda Games was a Shanghai online game developer, operator and publisher, best known for MMORPGs such as Legend of Mir 2 and Mir III. It was spun out of Shanda Interactive, founded in 2004 by Chen Tianqiao, and listed on Nasdaq (GAME) in 2009. It was taken private in 2015 by a consortium led by Shanda, and its assets later went to a Chinese-listed group. Consumer online games, strong in China, with little international brand awareness.

Skechers U.S.A. designs, makes and sells footwear and apparel under the Skechers name, spanning lifestyle, performance, running, walking, work and kids ranges, plus Skechers Hands Free Slip-ins. Sales go to consumers through wholesale, about 5,000 owned stores and e-commerce in over 170 countries, with annual revenue near 9 billion dollars. Based in Manhattan Beach, California and founded in 1992, it was listed on the NYSE (SKX) until 3G Capital took it private in 2025. It is a global consumer brand and a known sports sponsor.

Supreme is a New York streetwear brand founded in 1994 by James Jebbia, known for skate-influenced apparel, accessories and limited weekly drops under its red box logo, with collaborations with Louis Vuitton, Nike and The North Face. It sells to consumers through its own stores in cities such as New York, Los Angeles, London, Tokyo and Paris, plus online. It was acquired by VF Corporation in 2020 for 2.1 billion dollars, then sold to EssilorLuxottica in 2024 for about 1.5 billion dollars. A high-awareness consumer brand.

Sweetgreen is a Los Angeles-based fast casual restaurant chain serving salads, warm bowls and plates made with seasonal produce, sold through its app, delivery and over 250 restaurants in the US. Customers are mainly urban, health-conscious consumers, with revenue around 700 million dollars a year. It was founded in 2007 and listed on the NYSE (SG) in 2021. It acquired Spyce in 2021 to automate kitchens. It is a recognized US consumer brand with strong digital loyalty, though not widely known internationally.

Waha Capital is an Abu Dhabi investment company listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange. It invests across aviation leasing, financial services and asset management, real estate, industrials and consumer sectors, and has been tied to Abu Dhabi government-linked investors. Founded in 1997, it manages assets in the billions of dollars and has raised about 500 million dollars of capital, last in August 2021. It is a B2B and institutional investor with limited consumer visibility.

Yiguo.com is a Shanghai-based Chinese online fresh food and grocery e-commerce platform, selling fruit, vegetables, meat and seafood to urban consumers with cold chain delivery. Founded in 2008, it became one of China's largest fresh e-commerce operators and raised around 500 million dollars, with Alibaba among its investors. It is a consumer brand within China and has little recognition abroad.

Yimidida is a Shanghai online logistics network platform that matches shippers and freight carriers for less-than-truckload and full truckload transportation across China, supported by cloud data services. It earns fees from transport matching and logistics services. Customers are manufacturers, distributors and trucking operators. It raised about 540 million dollars, most recently in February 2020. It is a B2B logistics platform with little awareness outside China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Yingxiong Huyu, also known as Heroes Entertainment, is a Beijing developer and publisher of mobile esports games and related media, best known for the mobile MOBA Hero Mobile and esports tournaments in China. It earns money from in-game purchases, advertising and event rights. It raised about 3.6 billion yuan, last in September 2017. Its audience is young Chinese mobile gamers, and it has low brand awareness outside China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

1919 Wines & Spirits is a Chengdu, Sichuan, Chinese e-commerce liquor retailer selling baijiu, wine, whisky and other spirits through its website, apps, franchise stores and a delivery network. Founded in 2012, it serves consumers and restaurants, and has backing from Alibaba and other investors. It raised about 439 million dollars, last in October 2018, and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2024. It operates mainly in China, with moderate consumer awareness in the liquor trade.

Aiven is a Helsinki, Finland cloud data infrastructure company offering managed open source data services such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, Apache Kafka, ClickHouse, OpenSearch and Redis-compatible tools across AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and others. Customers are developers and enterprises paying usage-based fees. Founded in 2016, it has raised about 420 million dollars, with a 2022 round at a 2 billion dollar valuation. It is private. B2B, mainly known among developers and engineers, little consumer awareness.

American Eagle Outfitters is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania multi-brand specialty apparel retailer selling jeans, tops and accessories under American Eagle, Aerie intimates and the Todd Snyder menswear brand. Customers are young consumers shopping through about 1,100 stores and online across the US, Canada, Mexico and licensed international markets. Revenue is around 5 billion dollars. Founded in 1977, it is listed on the NYSE (AEO). Strong consumer brand, particularly among teens and college students in North America.

Asana is a San Francisco work management software company, founded in 2008 by Dustin Moskovitz and Justin Rosenstein. Its platform helps teams plan, track and automate projects and goals, with AI features. Customers are businesses and nonprofits, paying subscriptions, with revenue around 700 million dollars and over 100,000 paying customers in 190 countries. It direct-listed on the NYSE (ASAN) in 2020. It is a B2B brand with good awareness among office workers and has run sports sponsorships.

Benchling is a San Francisco cloud software company for life sciences R&D. Its platform covers molecular biology tools, lab notebooks, sample and workflow management, and data analysis used by biotech and pharma scientists. Customers include thousands of companies and academic labs, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2012 and valued at about 6.1 billion dollars in 2021, it raised around 410 million dollars. It is private. B2B with strong awareness among scientists and little consumer visibility.

Berkshire Grey is a Bedford, Massachusetts robotics company that built AI-driven robotic picking, sorting and parcel handling systems for e-commerce, retail and logistics warehouses. Customers included Walmart, Target, FedEx and Takeda, paying for systems and services. Founded in 2013, it raised about 428 million dollars and listed on Nasdaq (BGRY) via a SPAC merger in 2021. SoftBank acquired it in 2023 and took it private. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Betterment is a New York online investment adviser and robo-advisor, offering automated portfolios, retirement accounts, cash accounts and financial planning to individual savers plus a workplace 401(k) business and advisor platform. It earns advisory fees on assets, managing roughly 60 billion dollars for around a million customers. Founded in 2008, it has raised about 435 million dollars from investors including Kinnevik and Bessemer. It is private and a well-known US fintech consumer brand with heavy advertising.

BitSight is a Boston, Massachusetts cyber risk management company that rates the security posture of organizations using external data, with security ratings for third-party risk, cyber insurance and compliance. Customers are large enterprises, insurers and government bodies, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2011, it raised around 400 million dollars with a valuation reported above 2.4 billion dollars in 2021 and acquired Cybersixgill in 2024. It is private. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness.

Cable ONE, now branded Sparklight, is a Phoenix, Arizona provider of broadband internet, cable TV and phone services to residential and business customers in smaller US markets, across around 21 states, with roughly one million customers and revenue near 1.5 billion dollars. It also has investments in fixed wireless and fiber ventures such as MBI. Spun off from the Washington Post Company in 2015, it is listed on the NYSE (CABO). Regional consumer brand with limited national awareness.

Cellebrite is an Israeli-American digital intelligence firm, with US presence in Vienna, Virginia and main offices in Petah Tikva, Israel. It sells mobile forensics and data extraction tools such as UFED, plus cloud analytics, to police, intelligence, defense and corporate investigators in over 100 countries. Revenue is around 400 million dollars. Founded in 1999, it listed on Nasdaq (CLBT) in 2021 via a SPAC merger, with Sun Corporation as a major holder. B2B and government, with limited consumer awareness.

Chezhibao is a Nanjing, Jiangsu online used-car auction platform in China, linking dealers and buyers to auction and appraise vehicles, including trade-ins from 4S dealerships and leasing. Its revenue comes from auction transaction fees and related services. Backed by investors including Tencent, it raised about 387 million dollars, last in January 2019. It is a B2B auto-trade platform with little awareness outside China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Constant Contact is a Waltham, Massachusetts digital marketing platform for small businesses and nonprofits, selling email marketing, SMS, social media tools, websites and e-commerce tools by subscription. It has hundreds of thousands of small business customers, mostly in North America. Founded in 1995, it went public on Nasdaq in 2007, was bought by Endurance International in 2015, and later became part of Clearlake Capital-backed Stagwell-linked ownership; funding shown reflects those deals. B2B with moderate awareness among small business owners.

Datagroup-Volia and Lifecell is a Kyiv-based fixed and mobile telecoms operator created from the merger of Datagroup-Volia, a fixed broadband and cable TV provider, and Lifecell, one of Ukraine's three major mobile networks. It serves millions of residential, business and government customers and is owned by Turkey-related and Ukrainian groups, with Datagroup and Turkcell involved. It has raised about 435 million dollars, most recently in October 2024. A strong domestic consumer brand with no international presence.

Digital Turbine is an Austin, Texas mobile advertising and app distribution company. Its platforms (Ignite, Aurora, MobileFuse) pre-install and promote apps on Android phones for carriers and device makers, including Verizon, AT&T and Samsung, and sell app install advertising to developers. Revenue is around 500 to 600 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (APPS) after acquiring Mobile Posse, Fyber and AdColony. B2B, with low public awareness and little direct consumer branding.

Dotdash Meredith is a New York digital and print media company that owns brands including People, Better Homes and Gardens, Investopedia, Allrecipes, Southern Living, Real Simple, Verywell and Food and Wine. It generates revenue from advertising, licensing, commerce and subscriptions, reaching about 200 million people a month. Formed in 2021 when IAC's Dotdash acquired Meredith, it is owned by IAC, listed on Nasdaq (IAC), which acquired it fully. Its titles are widely recognized by US consumers.

Dragon is a Hong Kong-based blockchain and entertainment project describing itself as the world's number one entertainment coin, using the DRAGON token for gaming, gambling and wellness tie-ups in Macau and Asia. Its Crunchbase profile lists about 420 million dollars raised from an initial coin offering in January 2017. Customers are gaming and VIP casino users, and it earns from token use. Public information is thin and it has little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Eightfold AI is a Santa Clara, California software company whose AI-based Talent Intelligence Platform helps employers hire, retain and develop staff, using skills matching for recruiting, internal mobility and workforce planning. Customers are large enterprises paying subscriptions, including companies in tech, finance and retail. Founded in 2016 by Ashutosh Garg and Varun Kacholia, it raised about 400 million dollars, with a valuation of 2.1 billion dollars after its 2021 round led by SoftBank. B2B, limited consumer awareness.

Enerflex is a Calgary, Alberta energy infrastructure company that designs, builds, installs and services natural gas compression, processing and electric power equipment, and operates energy assets under long-term contracts. Customers are oil and gas producers and utilities across North America, Latin America, the Middle East and Australia. Revenue is around 2.5 billion Canadian dollars. Founded in 1980, it is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and NYSE (EFXT). It is an industrial B2B company with low consumer awareness.

Exabeam is a Broomfield, Colorado cybersecurity software company providing security information and event management, user and entity behavior analytics and AI-led threat detection and response. Customers are large enterprises and government bodies using its New-Scale SIEM platform. Founded in 2013, it merged with LogRhythm in 2024 and is owned by Thoma Bravo, having raised about 390 million dollars earlier. It is private. B2B, with limited public awareness outside security teams.

Formstack is a Denver, Colorado workplace productivity software company with online forms, documents and e-signature tools to automate data collection and workflows, under products such as Formstack Forms, Documents and Sign. Customers are businesses, schools and healthcare organizations paying subscriptions. Founded in 2006 in Indiana, it raised a 2021 growth investment of about 400 million dollars from Bain Capital Tech Opportunities, taking funding to roughly 425 million. B2B, with modest awareness among office users.

Foursquare is a location technology company based in San Francisco, with roots as a check-in app founded in 2009. Today it licenses location data, places datasets and developer tools, and sells advertising measurement and analytics under Foursquare Places, Movement and Audience, plus the consumer Swarm and Foursquare City Guide apps. Customers are marketers, mapping and app companies. It merged with Factual in 2020 and has raised about 394 million dollars. It is private. Known brand among tech users, but now mostly B2B.

Futu Clearing Inc. is a Dallas, Texas broker-dealer providing execution and clearing services for US securities, serving as the US clearing arm of Futu Holdings (Nasdaq: FUTU), which operates the Futu Niuniu and moomoo trading apps. It supports Futu's retail brokerage clients investing in US stocks and options. Capital reported is about 400 million dollars as of May 2021. It is a regulated subsidiary of Futu with little direct public brand recognition.

Future Lifestyle Fashions is a Mumbai-based Indian fashion retailer, part of Kishore Biyani's Future Group, operating apparel brands and formats such as Lee Cooper, Indigo Nation, Scullers, Central and Brand Factory in India. It sold apparel and accessories to consumers via department stores and e-commerce. It raised about 390 million dollars, including investment from Warburg Pincus. It was listed on Indian exchanges (NSE, BSE) but entered insolvency proceedings after Future Group's collapse and the failed Reliance deal. Familiar Indian consumer brands.

Grocery Outlet is an Emeryville, California extreme-value grocery retailer selling name-brand and private label food, produce, dairy, wine and general merchandise at steep discounts, with opportunistic buys of overstock. It has about 500 stores run by independent owner-operators in states such as California, Pennsylvania and the Pacific Northwest, with revenue around 4.5 billion dollars. It listed on Nasdaq (GO) in 2019 after being backed by Hellman and Friedman. Familiar US regional discount grocery brand.

Indegene Lifesystems is the Iselin, New Jersey US arm of Indegene, a healthcare technology and commercialization services company founded in India in 1998 and headquartered in Bengaluru. It provides analytics, medical, regulatory and commercial services to pharmaceutical, biotech and medical device firms globally, with revenue around 300 million dollars. Indegene listed on the NSE and BSE in India in 2024; Carlyle holds a stake. A B2B brand with low public awareness.

Industrious is a New York flexible workspace provider operating premium shared offices, private suites and meeting rooms across the US and some international sites, aimed at companies and individuals wanting managed space. Revenue comes from memberships and management agreements with landlords. Founded in 2012, it had 200 plus locations and raised about 420 million dollars. CBRE acquired it in 2025 for about 400 million dollars. A recognized business brand but limited consumer awareness.

International Transportation Service (ITS) is a Long Beach, California marine container terminal operator at the Port of Long Beach, handling container vessels, rail and truck movement for shipping lines. It is owned by Hong Kong-based Hutchison Ports. Customers are ocean carriers and cargo owners. A funding event of around 424 million dollars is shown for February 2025. It is a B2B port operator with essentially no consumer awareness.

Ipsos is a Paris-based global market research and consulting group, founded in 1975, providing surveys, polling, brand tracking, advertising testing and public opinion research. It operates in around 90 markets with about 20,000 employees and annual revenue of roughly 2.4 billion euros. Customers are consumer brands, governments and media. It is listed on Euronext Paris (IPS). Its polls are widely cited in news, but it is a B2B firm with little consumer branding.

John Cockerill Hydrogen is a Belgian maker of alkaline water electrolyzers for green hydrogen production, based in Seraing near Liege, and part of the John Cockerill Group, a Belgian engineering conglomerate with roots dating to 1817. It sells large electrolyzer systems and stacks to energy, industry and mobility project developers worldwide, with manufacturing in Belgium, France and China. It has raised about 346 million dollars, last in June 2025. B2B with little consumer awareness.

JumpCloud is a Louisville, Colorado cloud directory platform that lets IT teams manage user identities, devices (Windows, Mac, Linux, mobile), single sign-on, multi-factor authentication and access to apps and networks from one console. Customers are small and mid-size businesses and managed service providers worldwide, paying per-user subscriptions. Founded in 2012 by Rajat Bhargava, it has raised about 417 million dollars, with a valuation around 2.6 billion dollars in 2022. It is private. B2B, known among IT administrators, with little consumer awareness.

Katapult is a Plano, Texas fintech offering lease-to-own and point-of-sale payment options for consumers with limited credit, used to buy furniture, appliances, electronics and auto parts at online and in-store retailers. It earns lease fees and merchant partnerships. Founded in 2012 as Western Funding and rebranded, it listed on Nasdaq (KPLT) in 2021 via a SPAC merger with FinServ Acquisition Corp. US only. A retailer-embedded brand with modest consumer recognition.

Lamar Advertising is a Baton Rouge, Louisiana outdoor advertising company that owns and operates billboards, digital displays, transit and airport advertising, and logo signs along highways across the United States and Canada, with over 360,000 displays. Customers are local and national advertisers, who pay to rent space. Revenue is around 2.2 billion dollars. Founded in 1902, it is a real estate investment trust listed on Nasdaq (LAMR). A familiar roadside presence, but a B2B advertiser-facing brand.

LOGOS India is the Indian arm of LOGOS Property, an Asia Pacific logistics real estate investment and development platform headquartered in Singapore. It develops and manages warehouses and logistics parks for e-commerce, third-party logistics and retail tenants, with its India platform backed by Indian and global investors and based in Mumbai. About 400 million dollars of capital is shown. Customers are logistics and e-commerce occupiers. B2B real estate brand with little public awareness.

monday.com is a Tel Aviv work operating system company, founded in 2012, whose cloud platform lets teams build workflows for project management, CRM, software development and operations. It sells subscriptions to over 245,000 customers in 200 plus industries, with annual revenue above 1 billion dollars. It listed on Nasdaq (MNDY) in 2021. Heavy advertiser, including sports sponsorship, and well known among office and technology workers globally.

Moon Active is a Tel Aviv mobile games developer and publisher, best known for Coin Master, one of the highest-grossing mobile games, and Board Kings. Revenue comes from in-app purchases and advertising, with players worldwide and over a billion dollars in annual bookings. Founded in 2010, it raised about 425 million dollars, including a Viola-led round, and acquired Mobilityware's Solitaire Grand Harvest. It is private. Its games are widely downloaded but the company name is little known to the public.

Neovasc is a Richmond, British Columbia specialty medical device company that developed the Reducer, a device for refractory angina, and tissue products used in heart valves. Customers are hospitals and cardiologists, mainly in Europe. It was listed on Nasdaq (NVCN) and the TSX, and was acquired by Shockwave Medical in 2023, which sold the Reducer business to Johnson and Johnson MedTech via Shockwave's later acquisition in 2024. Funding shown is about 384 million dollars. B2B medical brand with no consumer awareness.

NotCo is a Santiago, Chile food technology company using an AI platform called Giuseppe to create plant-based versions of animal-based foods. Its consumer brands include NotMilk, NotBurger, NotMayo and NotIceCream, sold in Latin America, the US and other markets through retailers such as Whole Foods and Walmart, and it also licenses its AI to food manufacturers like Kraft Heinz. Founded in 2015, it raised about 433 million dollars and was valued at 1.5 billion dollars in 2021. Private. Recognized consumer brand in Latin America.

Postman is a San Francisco software company whose API platform helps developers design, test, document and monitor APIs, used by over 35 million developers and 500,000 organizations. It earns money from team and enterprise subscriptions. Founded in 2014 in Bangalore, India, it raised about 433 million dollars, with a 5.6 billion dollar valuation in 2021 led by Insight Partners. It is private. B2B, well known among software developers, with little general consumer awareness.

Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) is Pakistan's largest fixed-line telecoms and broadband operator, headquartered in Islamabad. It sells landline, DSL and fiber internet, Smart TV, and enterprise connectivity, and owns the Ufone mobile network through PTML. It was the state monopoly, privatised partly in 2006, when Etisalat bought 26 percent with management control; the Pakistani government holds about 62 percent. It is listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PTC). Strong national consumer brand and a sponsor of national cricket events.

Qiniu is a Shanghai cloud services company offering cloud storage, content delivery, live video and data processing services, and data lake and analytics tools for apps and enterprises. Customers include internet and media companies and developers across China. Founded in 2011, it raised about 397 million dollars from investors such as Alibaba and Tencent, and filed to list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. B2B, with limited public awareness outside China's developer community.

Signifyd is a San Jose, California e-commerce fraud protection company. Its platform decides in real time whether online orders are legitimate and guarantees against chargebacks, also handling returns abuse and account takeover. Customers are retailers and brands such as Peloton and Lacoste, who pay per-order fees. Founded in 2011, it raised about 409 million dollars, with a 1.3 billion dollar valuation in 2021. It is private. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Singapore Post is Singapore's national postal operator, headquartered in Singapore. It delivers mail and parcels, and runs e-commerce logistics, freight forwarding and international post services through its SingPost brand plus businesses in Australia and Asia, including logistics group Famous Holdings and Freight Links.
